{{nihongo|'''Iwai Shrine'''|磐井神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine ranking system}} its rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

Before the Edo period, it was also called '''Suzumori Hachimangū''' (Suzunomori Hachimangū / Suzugamori Hachimangū). It is also said to have been positioned as the "general Hachiman shrine of Musashi Province." In the precincts, {{ill|Benzaiten|qid=Q818468|lt=Benzaiten}} (Kasajima Benten Shrine), one of the "Tōkai Seven Lucky Gods," is enshrined.

=== History ===
Its founding date is unknown, but it is traditionally said to have been founded in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ar|الإمبراطور بيداتسو|arz|الامبراطور بيداتسو|azb|بیداتسو (ایمپیراتور)|cs|Bidacu|de|Bidatsu|es|Bidatsu Tennō|fa|امپراتور بیداتسو|fi|Bidatsu|fr|Bidatsu|id|Kaisar Bidatsu|it|Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇|ka|ბიდაცუ|ko|비다쓰 천황|mr|बिदात्सु|nl|Bidatsu|pl|Bidatsu|pt|Bidatsu|ru|Император Бидацу|sh|Car Bidatsu|simple|Emperor Bidatsu|sl|Cesar Bidacu|sv|Bidatsu|th|จักรพรรดิบิดัตสึ|tl|Emperador Bidatsu|tr|Bidatsu|uk|Імператор Бідацу|uz|Imperator Bidatsu|vi|Thiên hoàng Bidatsu|yo|Emperor Bidatsu|zh|敏达天皇|zh_min_nan|Bidatu Thian-hông|zh_yue|敏達天皇|qid=Q316637}}{{sfn|Tokyo Metropolitan Association of Shinto Shrines}}. According to the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}, in {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 1 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}) it is recorded that "Iwai Shrine of Musashi Province, Junior Fifth Rank, was listed as an official shrine." In the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, it was also listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}. It is also said to have been designated the general Hachiman shrine ({{ill|Kokubu-Hachimangu|ja|国府八幡宮|qid=Q11420856|lt=Sōsha Hachimangū}}) of {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}}.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it received the devotion of the shogunal house and was also called "Suzugamori Hachiman(gū)"{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō, Irido Village}}. The place name Suzugamori is said to come from the "bell stone" passed down at this shrine (a stone that rings like a {{ill|suzu|de|Schelle (Klangkörper)|ja|鈴|sv|Bjällra|zh|铃|zh_yue|啷啷|qid=Q7651136}}).
